paper_id: Ma et al. - 2011 - Opportunistic concurrency A MAC protocol for wireless sensor networks
title: Opportunistic Concurrency: A MAC Protocol for Wireless Sensor Networks
motivation: CSMA defers transmission when channel busy, missing opportunities for parallel transmission in WSNs with heavy traffic.
problem_framing: Enabling opportunistic concurrent transmissions using MIM physical capability with only local information at each node.
key_insight: CSMA's channel-busy rule is overly conservative; SINR conditions at receivers determine success, not carrier sense alone.
method_signature: Local concurrency map + SINR-based decision algorithm integrated with X-MAC for distributed transmission decisions.
evaluation_criteria: Latency reduction, throughput increase, energy reduction on 60 TelosB testbed vs CSMA baseline.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: When Cmax > 2, collision mostly happens and performance decreases. OPC slightly increases retransmission cases.
evidence_for_taste: not to enforce any transmission with high signal strength
we didn’t allow any transmission decision that will result in any other transmission failure
when we allow 3 or 4 transmissions concurrently proceed, collision mostly happens
the throughput does not monotonically increase with Cmax
OPC slightly increases the retransmission cases
the harm of hidden terminal brought by OPC is quite little
thinking_moves: 识别物理层新能力(MIM)改变了原本不可行的约束条件
把serial transmission优化问题重新frame成parallel transmission机会挖掘
用局部信息(concurrency map)替代全局协调实现分布式决策
承认追求并发会引入hidden terminal，但权衡收益大于危害
